headline: Microsoft plans to let Teams meetings use outside deepfake-detection tools and to warn users about suspected impersonators, with release due in November.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a concrete product plan against meeting fraud, but it is a roadmap entry with no results yet.
importance_line: Companies that run video meetings on Teams will get warnings about fake or manipulated participants, which targets fraud using synthetic voices and faces, but it is still a plan from a roadmap, and detection quality depends on the third-party tools used.
summary: BleepingComputer reports, from new entries on the Microsoft 365 Roadmap, that Microsoft is developing support for certified third-party tools that analyse meeting audio and video for signs of synthetic or manipulated content and send warnings into Teams, plus an impersonation-protection feature that flags suspected fake organisers or participants. Both are listed as due for general availability in November 2026 after a worldwide rollout.
notes: Read in full on BleepingComputer; the Microsoft 365 Roadmap entries were not opened.
